title: An idea about shelf–slope physical–ecosystem coupling
reference_mode: Open-ended hypothesis testing; no unique gold hypothesis, expected result sign or target figure.
reference_text:
Apply each criterion's specific 0-4 anchors. Assess scientific value and the explained extension, comparison, synthesis or boundary test, not worldwide first discovery. A related idea already studied elsewhere is not automatically penalized. Mere restatement of a supplied conclusion is insufficient; changing years alone is not a scientific rationale. No predetermined example hypothesis is a target answer. A supported, contradicted or genuinely unresolved hypothesis can receive full credit. Demand adequate testing and evidence, not a positive finding. Cite source and submission locations and mark unavailable verification; never invent source passages, unseen images or a successful replay. Technical checks use the selected hypothesis and frozen inputs, not paper values as ground truth. Do not demand extra fields or the reference papers' full model experiments.

Task-specific interpretation limits: Restrict the primary test to supplied chlorophyll, temperature, salinity and velocity support. An association with transport does not measure nutrient supply or biological production directly. No nutrient budget or a particular mechanism/sign is prescribed. No typhoon attribution or full process budget is required; I1 does not include verified storm tracks, winds or budget diagnostics.
Data alignment: Two readings share the South China Sea CMOMS framework; the newer northern-shelf study uses different observations and idealized experiments. All relate to the region, but neither files nor years are identical to I1.

Use related-work source texts supplied separately to verify literature fidelity. This JSON contains bibliographic screening notes, not substitutes for the full texts. The current judge helper does not automatically load this reading pack or perform replay.

criteria.title: Faithful reading of related work
criteria.description: Check the central claims the submission relies on against the supplied papers; distinguish observation, model result, association and proposed mechanism.

anchors.0: No relevant literature evidence, or central attribution is fabricated.
anchors.1: Names papers but substantially misstates their central method, finding or evidential status.
anchors.2: Mostly recognizes the topic, but a material method, limitation or attribution is wrong or unsupported.
anchors.3: Accurately describes the relied-on findings and methods with traceable citations; only a minor limitation is omitted.
anchors.4: Accurately links relied-on findings, methods and limitations to source passages and distinguishes findings from hypotheses; no material misrepresentation.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Source passages and the submission passages that interpret them.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Scientific value and development of the idea
criteria.description: Assess why the proposed question is worth testing and how the readings inform an extension, comparison, synthesis or boundary test. Do not require an unprecedented mechanism or method.

anchors.0: No research question or scientific rationale is offered; the submission only restates a supplied finding.
anchors.1: Proposes a topic or rerun but gives no substantive reason why the test is useful.
anchors.2: States a feasible question and a link to the readings, but the scientific value or informative comparison is weak.
anchors.3: Explains a scientifically meaningful extension, comparison, synthesis or boundary test grounded in the readings, even if a related idea has been studied elsewhere.
anchors.4: Clearly explains what the test can teach, distinguishes relevant competing expectations or applicability conditions, and develops a feasible question from the readings without exaggerated novelty claims.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Research rationale, connection to the supplied studies, and explanation of the information gained by the proposed test.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Operationally specific hypothesis
criteria.description: Look for one primary hypothesis with a defined population/domain, response, predictor or comparison, scale and expected relationship.

anchors.1: Only a broad topic or an unmeasurable claim is offered.
anchors.2: An expected relationship is stated but key variables, scale or target population remain ambiguous.
anchors.3: A specific primary relationship and measurable variables/domain are defined, with a minor operational omission.
anchors.4: One primary hypothesis specifies observable quantities, domain/scale and predicted contrast or relationship sufficiently for another analyst to implement the test.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Primary hypothesis and operational variable definitions.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Falsification and decision rule
criteria.description: Distinguish support, contradiction and insufficient evidence; a non-significant test alone is not proof of no effect.

anchors.0: The claim is unfalsifiable or no test outcome could count against it.
anchors.1: Mentions validation but gives no measurable rejection or contradiction condition.
anchors.2: Offers a test and vague decision threshold, but conflates non-significance with absence or leaves direction/meaning unclear.
anchors.3: Defines interpretable support/contradiction conditions and recognizes inconclusive results; one threshold or practical-effect detail is weak.
anchors.4: Defines an appropriate decision rule before the main test, including effect direction or relevant magnitude and uncertainty, and distinguishes contradiction from inadequate information.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Dated plan or early run record, decision rule, and final interpretation.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Feasibility and analysis chronology
criteria.description: Reward appropriate data inspection and transparent exploration; do not pretend a hypothesis was specified before analysis without a record.

anchors.0: The hypothesis requires unavailable essential measurements or no feasible analysis is attempted.
anchors.1: Assumes unavailable variables, resolution or independent samples without acknowledging the issue.
anchors.2: Shows partial feasibility but important support constraints or exploratory versus confirmatory use are unclear.
anchors.3: Checks needed variables, domain and sampling; records the hypothesis before the main test or clearly labels exploration, with minor omissions.
anchors.4: Demonstrates data support, records the primary plan and revisions in order, and separates data-driven discovery from an independent check where claimed; limitations and fallback scope are explicit.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Input inspection, plan timestamp/order, revisions, and exploratory/validation split where applicable.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Informative baseline or comparator
criteria.description: The comparator must distinguish the claim under comparable data support; a complicated model is not required.

anchors.0: No comparator or a comparator incapable of testing the claimed advantage/contrast.
anchors.1: Uses an obviously weak or mismatched comparator that favors the hypothesis.
anchors.2: A relevant comparator exists but differing support, tuning or definitions materially confound the comparison.
anchors.3: A defensible baseline/control uses comparable samples and metrics; minor fairness details are missing.
anchors.4: A justified baseline or control directly tests the scientific contrast on comparable support, with equally treated preprocessing/tuning and an interpretable effect estimate.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Comparator definition, matched sample support and paired result.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Alternative explanations and confounding
criteria.description: Assess plausible alternatives for the chosen hypothesis, not a mandatory list of every conceivable confounder.

anchors.0: Treats an association as proof of mechanism with no consideration of alternatives.
anchors.1: Lists generic confounders but does not relate them to this analysis.
anchors.2: Identifies a relevant alternative and makes a partial adjustment, leaving a major identifiable ambiguity unexamined.
anchors.3: Uses an appropriate comparison or adjustment for a key alternative and limits remaining causal claims.
anchors.4: Actively tests a plausible competing explanation using defensible stratification, matching, controls or equivalent analysis, explains assumptions, and retains limits on causal identification.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Named alternative, discriminatory analysis and assumptions.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Uncertainty and effective sample support
criteria.description: The independent unit can be a year, event, float or spatial block, not automatically every pixel or daily observation.

anchors.0: No uncertainty assessment, or fundamentally invalid inference drives the conclusion.
anchors.1: Reports significance or confidence while treating strongly dependent samples as independent without justification.
anchors.2: Quantifies uncertainty but only partly handles temporal/spatial dependence, imbalance or sparse events.
anchors.3: Uses justified uncertainty estimates and dependence-aware sampling/inference; minor effective-support reporting gaps remain.
anchors.4: Quantifies effect size and uncertainty with a defensible independent unit and dependence-aware method; reports support and handles sparse events or low power honestly.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Uncertainty computation, sampling units, event/sample counts and intervals or equivalent estimates.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Robustness, selection and leakage
criteria.description: Prediction claims need genuinely held-out evaluation; non-predictive claims need an appropriate independent/robustness check rather than an arbitrary train/test split.

anchors.0: Test leakage, cherry-picking or an unacknowledged search invalidates the main evidence.
anchors.1: Only reports a favorable specification or random splits despite clear dependent-sample leakage.
anchors.2: Attempts a robustness or validation check but leaves a major selection/leakage issue.
anchors.3: Uses a relevant sensitivity or independent check, keeps tuning separate where needed and reports explored choices with minor gaps.
anchors.4: Tests the conclusion against a relevant alternate specification or independent block, prevents information leakage where applicable, and discloses selection/search with correction or explicitly exploratory interpretation.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Validation/sensitivity results, preprocessing fit scope, split definitions and analysis-choice record.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Correct input handling and derived variables
criteria.description: Audit metadata, units, coordinates, temporal alignment, missingness and relevant geometry. Only demand checks material to the selected analysis.

anchors.0: Uses the wrong data or a fundamental unit/geometry/alignment error invalidates the result.
anchors.1: Several major preprocessing errors or unverified substitutions affect the analysis.
anchors.2: Core inputs are appropriate but a material conversion, support or alignment check is missing or partly wrong.
anchors.3: Relevant units, geometry, alignment and missingness are correctly handled with minor documentation gaps.
anchors.4: Correctly handles the frozen input conventions and all material transformations, with inspectable checks that rule out misleading support or alignment artifacts.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Input manifest, transformation code, spot checks and validity masks.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Correct execution of the selected analysis
criteria.description: There is no fixed scientific answer; independently check whether the submitted method was implemented and computed correctly.

anchors.0: No executed test, fabricated results, or the core calculation is demonstrably wrong.
anchors.1: Code/results show major departures from the stated method or unsupported numerical claims.
anchors.2: A meaningful calculation was performed but an important implementation or numerical verification gap remains.
anchors.3: Implementation and reported values are consistent with the stated method; independent checks cover central computations with only minor gaps.
anchors.4: Independent recalculation or equivalent trusted checks verify the central statistics, comparisons and figure values; formulas, masks, thresholds and reported numbers agree.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Executed code/results and independent numerical audit. Textual confidence or plotted shape alone cannot establish full credit.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Reproducible execution
criteria.description: Do not infer execution from a notebook's existence or stored outputs; preserve one coherent analysis rather than demand a notebook per result.

anchors.0: No usable calculation code or execution evidence.
anchors.1: Fragments or inaccessible dependencies prevent reconstructing the main analysis.
anchors.2: Substantial code exists but missing settings, paths or steps prevent reliable rerun.
anchors.3: Complete code, input references and environment/settings are supplied and consistent with results, but independent clean replay is absent or has a minor unresolved issue.
anchors.4: An independently recorded clean replay from the frozen inputs regenerates the central analysis within declared numerical tolerance using the supplied code and environment/settings.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Code/notebook, dependency/settings record, original execution evidence and separate replay log if available.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Calibrated scientific conclusion
criteria.description: Support, contradiction and inconclusive evidence can all receive full credit; successful prediction or a positive finding is not the scoring target.

anchors.0: Conclusion contradicts the results, is fabricated, or claims a result without a test.
anchors.1: Strong claims ignore obvious null/contradictory findings or major limitations.
anchors.2: Broad conclusion follows part of the evidence but overstates causality, certainty or generality.
anchors.3: Conclusion tracks the primary result and acknowledges relevant limits; only a minor overstatement remains.
anchors.4: Conclusion follows the declared test and uncertainty, includes inconvenient results, distinguishes association/prediction/causality and limits generalization to supported data.

criteria.evidence_requirements: Main effect/uncertainty, decision rule and conclusion passages.
criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

criteria.title: Traceable and interpretable evidence
criteria.description: Reward sufficient evidence for the chosen test, not a prescribed number of figures or report length.

anchors.0: No inspectable evidence supports the central claim.
anchors.1: Figures/tables or citations cannot be linked to the stated result.
anchors.2: Some links are traceable but key quantities, labels, sample support or result locations are unclear.
anchors.3: Central claims link to understandable numerical/visual evidence with minor labeling or provenance gaps.
anchors.4: Each central claim points to clearly labeled, unit-aware numerical or visual evidence and its generating calculation; data gaps and comparison support are visible where consequential.

criteria.source_basis: OceanX benchmark evaluation design, not a scoring rule claimed to be authored by the related-work papers.

visual_scoring_policy.comparison_target: Scientific clarity and evidence traceability, not pixel similarity or number of plots.
visual_scoring_policy.full_credit: Use evidence appropriate to the chosen hypothesis; no fixed plot count or expected sign. Judge quantitative correctness under C2 and communication under E2.
visual_scoring_policy.uninspected_images: Unseen figures are unverified, not inferred from captions.

scoring.weight_origin: User-approved category weights expanded into 14 benchmark-designed anchored items.
scoring.unknowns: Score only demonstrated evidence and explicitly identify missing source/execution information; lack of verification is not an assertion of fabrication.
scoring.no_double_counting: Explain item-specific consequences; do not mechanically repeat one deduction across all items.

related_work_basis.title: Nutrient transport and dynamics in the South China Sea: A modeling study
related_work_basis.relevance: Provides a CMOMS physical-biogeochemical context for South China Sea chlorophyll and transport.
related_work_basis.limitation: The climatological experiment is not identical to the proposed 2018-2022 historical archive. Nutrient budgets require extra fields not supplied here.
related_work_basis.source_dataset: CMOMS South China Sea coupled physical-biogeochemical experiment; climatological final model years, not dated historical files.

related_work_basis.title: A Modeling Study of Nutrient Transport and Dynamics Over the Northern Slope of the South China Sea
related_work_basis.relevance: Shares the CMOMS South China Sea framework and focuses on northern-slope transport and ecosystem structure.
related_work_basis.limitation: Same model system does not establish byte-identical output or forcing; the historical-window test is an explicit transfer. No unprovided nutrient flux is compulsory.
related_work_basis.source_dataset: CMOMS/ROMS nitrogen-phosphorus biological module; northern South China Sea slope; Methods identifies the model framework and links the Lu2020 validation.

related_work_basis.title: Typhoon-induced surface chlorophyll a decline on the shelf of the South China Sea
related_work_basis.source_dataset: Northern SCS shelf; OC-CCI v6.0, 4 km/8-day chlorophyll and IBTrACS tracks for 2001–2023; 2016 cruise context and idealized Nida-based experiments. Same CMOMS model identity is not established.
related_work_basis.relevance: Provides a counterexample to uniform positive ecosystem responses, connecting shelf context, transport and vertical structure.
related_work_basis.limitation: These observations and idealized experiments are not I1. No typhoon tracks, winds, nutrient fields or budget terms are added; event attribution requires inputs absent from I1.

task_selection_rationale: Keep the same-model transport foundation and add a recent regional counterexample that can inspire questions about context-dependent responses. The agent chooses its own feasible question, not a required typhoon experiment.

evaluator_protocol.adjudication: Review disagreements of at least two anchor levels on any item and critical leakage/numerical-error disagreements.
evaluator_protocol.implementation_status: Protocol only; source-pack staging, independent numerical/replay audits and two-judge orchestration are not automated by this change.

release_requirements: Stage and fully review the selected complete source texts for both agents; verify bibliographic identity, local file hashes and evaluator-readable source locations. Abstract screening alone is insufficient.
Obtain authorized data, verify variables/sample support and freeze masks, processing, file hashes and the input contract before runs.
Freeze query and reading-pack fingerprints; do not silently update papers after an attempt.
Calibrate item anchors on pilot submissions and confirm identical budgets, tool access and literature policy for both systems.
Prepare independent numerical and execution-audit procedures for agent-selected analyses, without inventing a single gold hypothesis or demanding the published conclusion.
Confirm evaluator evidence fits configured limits without silent truncation; a single-judge API call does not perform full-source reading or clean replay automatically.
Only mark validated after release checks are actually satisfied; retain originals, failures, judge disagreement and adjudication records.
reading_data_alignment: Two readings share the South China Sea CMOMS framework; the newer northern-shelf study uses different observations and idealized experiments. All relate to the region, but neither files nor years are identical to I1.
reading_inspiration: Regional transport foundations paired with a context-dependent ecological response.
